metadata.title: Another approach to non-repetitive colorings of graphs of bounded degree

nodes.name: Square (sequence)
nodes.statement: A sequence $s_1\ldots s_{2n}$ is a $\emph{square}$ if $s_i=s_{i+n}$ for each $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: A sequence is a square if its first and second halves are identical.

nodes.name: Repetitive / non-repetitive (square-free) sequence
nodes.statement: A sequence is $\emph{repetitive}$ if it contains a consecutive subsequence that is a square; otherwise it is $\emph{non-repetitive}$ (or $\emph{square-free}$).

nodes.name: Non-repetitive coloring of a graph
nodes.statement: A coloring (of vertices or edges) of a graph $G$ is $\emph{non-repetitive}$ if the sequence of colors induced by every path of $G$ is non-repetitive.

nodes.name: Thue number $\pi(G)$ and Thue index $\pi'(G)$
nodes.statement: The Thue number $\pi(G)$ (resp. Thue index $\pi'(G)$) is the smallest number of colors in a non-repetitive vertex (resp. edge) coloring of $G$.

nodes.name: List assignment and non-repetitive $l$-choosability
nodes.statement: A list assignment $L$ maps each vertex $v$ (and/or edge) to a color set $L(v)$. $G$ is non-repetitively $L$-colorable if it admits a non-repetitive coloring with $c(v)\in L(v)$; non-repetitively $l$-choosable if this holds for every $L$ with $|L(v)|\ge l$.

nodes.name: Thue choice number $\pi_{\operatorname{ch}}(G)$ and choice index $\pi'_{\operatorname{ch}}(G)$
nodes.statement: $\pi_{\operatorname{ch}}(G)$ is the smallest $l$ such that $G$ is non-repetitively $l$-choosable; $\pi'_{\operatorname{ch}}(G)$ is the edge-list analogue.

nodes.name: Weak total Thue coloring
nodes.statement: A coloring of edges and vertices of $G$ is a $\emph{weak total Thue coloring}$ if the sequence of consecutive vertex- and edge-colors of every path is non-repetitive.

nodes.name: Total Thue coloring
nodes.statement: A coloring is a (strong) $\emph{total Thue coloring}$ if both the sequence of vertex-colors and the sequence of edge-colors of every path are non-repetitive.

nodes.name: Weak/total Thue numbers and choice numbers
nodes.statement: $\pi_{\operatorname{T_w}}(G)$ (resp. $\pi_{\operatorname{T}}(G)$) is the minimum number of colors in a weak (resp. strong) total Thue coloring; $\pi_{\operatorname{T_wch}}(G)$ and $\pi_{\operatorname{Tch}}(G)$ are the list-coloring counterparts.

nodes.name: Vertex-paths, edge-paths, mixed-paths
nodes.statement: A $\emph{vertex-path}$ (resp. $\emph{edge-path}$) is a sequence of consecutive adjacent vertices (resp. edges); a $\emph{mixed-path}$ is an alternating sequence of vertices and edges with consecutive elements adjacent. All paths are simple.

nodes.name: $C_L(G)$ — set of valid colorings
nodes.statement: For a graph $G$ and list assignment $L$, $C_L(G)$ denotes the set of valid (non-repetitive / weak total / total Thue) colorings of $G$ respecting $L$; the notion of validity is fixed by context.

nodes.name: Thue choice number of a path
nodes.statement: For every path $P$, $\pi_{\operatorname{ch}}(P)=4$.

nodes.name: Doubling lemma for paths
nodes.statement: Let $L$ be a list assignment of a path $P$ with all lists of size $4$, and let $C_n$ count non-repetitive $L$-colorings of the $n$ leftmost vertices. Then for every $n<|P|$, $C_{n+1}\ge 2C_n$.
assumptions: $L$ is a list assignment of path $P$ with $|L(v)|=4$ for every vertex $v$

nodes.name: Proof of doubling lemma for paths
nodes.statement: By induction on $n$: bound $|F|$ (the colorings of the $n+1$ leftmost vertices that are repetitive but extend a valid coloring of the $n$ leftmost) using $|F_i|\le 2^{1-i}C_n$, then sum the geometric series.

nodes.name: Set up induction and split $|F|$
nodes.statement: Proceed by induction on $n$; let $F$ be the set of colorings of the $n+1$ leftmost vertices that respect $L$, are repetitive, but induce a non-repetitive coloring of the $n$ leftmost. Then $C_{n+1}=4C_n-|F|$.

nodes.name: Bound $|F_i|$ via induction hypothesis
nodes.statement: Let $F_i\subset F$ contain a square of length $2i$. The last $i$ colors are determined by the previous $i$, so $|F_i|\le C_{n+1-i}$, and the IH gives $|F_i|\le 2^{1-i}C_n$.

nodes.name: Sum the geometric series
nodes.statement: $C_{n+1}\ge 4C_n-\sum_{i\ge1}2^{1-i}C_n\ge 2C_n$.

nodes.name: Improved Thue choice number bound
nodes.statement: For every graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta\ge 1$, $\pi_{\operatorname{ch}}(G)\le\Delta^2+\frac{3}{2^{2/3}}\Delta^{5/3}+2^{2/3}\Delta^{4/3}$.
assumptions: $G$ is a graph with maximum degree $\Delta\ge 1$

nodes.name: Multiplicative growth lemma for non-repetitive list colorings
nodes.statement: Let $\Delta\ge2$, $\gamma=\frac{3}{2^{2/3}}+2^{2/3}\Delta^{-1/3}+\Delta^{-2/3}$. If $G$ has max degree $\le\Delta$ and every list of $L$ has size $\ge\Delta(\Delta-1)(1+\gamma\Delta^{-1/3})+1$, then for every vertex $v$, $|C_L(G)|\ge\Delta(\Delta-1)(1+2^{1/3}\Delta^{-1/3})|C_L(G\setminus\{v\})|$.

nodes.name: Proof of multiplicative growth lemma (non-repetitive)
nodes.statement: By induction on $|V(G)|$: count repetitive extensions $F$ via paths of length $2i$ through $v$, bound $|F_i|$ using path counts $i\Delta(\Delta-1)^{2i-2}$ and the IH, sum the resulting series, and substitute $\gamma$.

nodes.name: Base case and induction setup
nodes.statement: Induction on $|V(G)|$. Base $|G|=1$ is immediate. Define $F$ as colorings of $G$ respecting $L$ that are repetitive yet induce a non-repetitive coloring of $G\setminus\{v\}$, giving $|C_L(G)|=(\Delta(\Delta-1)(1+\gamma\Delta^{-1/3})+1)|C_L(G\setminus\{v\})|-|F|$.

nodes.name: Decompose $F$ by square length and bound $|C_L(G\setminus p')|$ via IH
nodes.statement: Let $F_i$ be colorings in $F$ containing a path of length $2i$ that is a square. The half $p'$ containing $v$ has $i$ vertices, so by IH, $|C_L(G\setminus p')|\le|C_L(G\setminus\{v\})|/(\Delta(\Delta-1)(1+2^{1/3}\Delta^{-1/3}))^{i-1}$.

nodes.name: Count paths through $v$
nodes.statement: There are at most $i\Delta(\Delta-1)^{2i-2}$ paths of length $2i$ through $v$: choose the length of the shorter half ($0$ to $i-1$), then build by DFS with $\Delta$ choices for the first vertex and $\Delta-1$ for each other.

nodes.name: Combine bounds for $|F_i|$ and split $i=1$ vs $i\ge2$
nodes.statement: $|F_i|\le i\Delta(\Delta-1)^{2i-2}|C_L(G\setminus\{v\})|/(\Delta(\Delta-1)(1+2^{1/3}\Delta^{-1/3}))^{i-1}$. For $i\ge2$ this gives $|F_i|\le i(\Delta-1)|C_L(G\setminus\{v\})|/(1+2^{1/3}\Delta^{-1/3})^{i-1}$; for $i=1$, $|F_1|\le\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{v\})|$.

nodes.name: Sum the geometric series
nodes.statement: $|F|\le|C_L(G\setminus\{v\})|(1+(\Delta-1)\Delta^{2/3}(2^{-1/3}+\Delta^{-1/3})^2)$ using $\sum_{i\ge1}i x^{i-1}/(1-x)^{-2}$ identity.

nodes.name: Substitute $\gamma$ and conclude
nodes.statement: Substituting $\gamma=\frac{3}{2^{2/3}}+2^{2/3}\Delta^{-1/3}+\Delta^{-2/3}$ yields $|C_L(G)|\ge|C_L(G\setminus\{v\})|\Delta(\Delta-1)(1+2^{1/3}\Delta^{-1/3})$.

nodes.name: Weak total Thue choice number bound (linear)
nodes.statement: For every graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta\ge 1$, $\pi_{\operatorname{T_wch}}(G)\le 6\Delta$.
assumptions: $G$ is a graph with maximum degree $\Delta\ge 1$

nodes.name: Multiplicative growth lemma for weak total Thue colorings
nodes.statement: Let $\Delta\ge 2$. If $G$ has max degree $<\Delta$ and every list has size $\ge 6\Delta$, then for any vertex or edge $x$ of $G$, $|C_L(G)|\ge 3\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|$.
assumptions: $x$ is any vertex or edge of $G$

nodes.name: Proof of multiplicative growth lemma for weak total Thue
nodes.statement: By induction on $|V|+|E|$: bound colorings $F$ that fail via mixed-paths of length $2i$ through $x$, count such mixed-paths $\le i\Delta^i$, sum $\sum i/3^{i-1}=9/4$, and conclude $|C_L(G)|\ge\frac{15}{4}\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|\ge 3\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|$.

nodes.name: Induction setup and definition of $F$
nodes.statement: Induct on $|V|+|E|$. Define $F$ as colorings respecting $L$ that are weak-total-repetitive yet induce a weak total Thue coloring of $G\setminus\{x\}$, so $|C_L(G)|=6\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|-|F|$.

nodes.name: Decompose $F$ via mixed-paths and apply IH
nodes.statement: Let $F_i$ be colorings of $F$ containing a mixed-path of length $2i$ inducing a square. By IH, $|C_L(G\setminus p')|\le|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|/(3\Delta)^{i-1}$.

nodes.name: Count mixed-paths through $x$
nodes.statement: If $x$ is a vertex, $\le i\Delta^i$ mixed-paths of length $2i$ through $x$; if $x$ is an edge, $\le 2i\Delta^{i-1}\le i\Delta^i$.

nodes.name: Sum series to bound $|F|$
nodes.statement: $|F_i|\le i\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|/3^{i-1}$, hence $|F|\le\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|\sum_{i\ge1}i/3^{i-1}=\frac{9}{4}\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: $|C_L(G)|\ge 6\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|-\frac{9}{4}\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|=\frac{15}{4}\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|\ge 3\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|$.

nodes.name: Weak total Thue choice number bound for large $\Delta$
nodes.section: 4.2 Weak total Thue coloring for large maximal degree
nodes.statement: For every graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta\ge 300$, $\pi_{\operatorname{T_wch}}(G)\le\lceil 4.25\Delta\rceil$.
assumptions: $G$ is a graph with maximum degree $\Delta\ge 300$

nodes.name: Two-rate growth lemma for weak total Thue colorings
nodes.statement: Let $\Delta\ge 300$. If $G$ has max degree $<\Delta$ and every list has size $\ge 4.25\Delta$, then for any vertex $v$, $|C_L(G)|\ge 1.62\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{v\})|$, and for any edge $e$, $|C_L(G)|\ge 4.2\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{e\})|$.

nodes.name: Proof of two-rate growth lemma
nodes.statement: Same induction as LP424.3 but with two growth rates: for an edge use $\le 2i\Delta^{i-1}$ paths and rate $1.62\Delta$; for a vertex, the half $p'$ contains $\ge\lceil(i-1)/2\rceil$ edges so the IH gives factor $(\sqrt{1.62\cdot 4.2}\Delta)^{i-1}$. Numerics for $\Delta>300$ close both bounds.

nodes.name: Edge case: $x=e$
nodes.statement: Use $\le 2i\Delta^{i-1}$ mixed-paths through $e$ and $|C_L(G)|\ge 1.62\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|$ for all elements; numerical computation for $\Delta>300$ gives $|C_L(G)|\ge 4.2\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{e\})|$.

nodes.name: Vertex case: $x=v$ with mixed exponents
nodes.statement: If $v$ is a vertex, the half $p'$ of a mixed-path of length $2i$ contains $\ge\lceil(i-1)/2\rceil$ edges, so IH yields $|C_L(G\setminus p')|\le|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|/(\sqrt{1.62\cdot 4.2}\,\Delta)^{i-1}$; with $\le i\Delta^i$ paths the series gives $|C_L(G)|\ge 1.62\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{v\})|$.

nodes.name: Total Thue choice number bound
nodes.statement: For every graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta$, $\pi_{\operatorname{Tch}}(G)\le\Delta^2+\frac{3}{2^{1/3}}\Delta^{5/3}+8\Delta^{4/3}+1$.
assumptions: $G$ is a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$

nodes.name: Multiplicative growth lemma for total Thue colorings
nodes.statement: Let $\Delta\ge 2$, $\gamma=\frac{3}{2^{1/3}}+8\Delta^{-1/3}$. If $G$ has max degree $<\Delta$ and every list has size $\ge\Delta^2(1+\gamma\Delta^{-1/3})$, then for any vertex or edge $x$, $|C_L(G)|\ge\Delta^2(1+2^{2/3}\Delta^{-1/3})|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|$.
assumptions: $x$ is a vertex or edge of $G$

nodes.name: Proof of multiplicative growth lemma for total Thue
nodes.statement: Induct on $|V|+|E|$. Decompose $F=\bigcup(M_i\cup S_i)$ where $M_i$ uses mixed-paths and $S_i$ uses pure edge-/vertex-paths of length $2i$. Bound counts and sum series, then substitute $\gamma$.

nodes.name: Induction setup; split $F$ into $M_i\cup S_i$
nodes.statement: Induct on $|V|+|E|$. $F$ = colorings respecting $L$ that are not total Thue but induce one on $G\setminus\{x\}$. $M_i$: $F$-colorings with a mixed-path of length $2i$ inducing a square; $S_i$: with an edge-path (resp. vertex-path) if $x$ is an edge (resp. vertex). $|F|\le\sum_{i\ge1}(|M_i|+|S_i|)$.

nodes.name: Bound $|M_i|$ via mixed-path counts
nodes.statement: For mixed-paths: at most $i\Delta^i$ through $x$, IH gives factor $(\Delta^2(1+2^{2/3}\Delta^{-1/3}))^{i-1}$, so $|M_i|\le i\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|/(\Delta(1+2^{2/3}\Delta^{-1/3}))^{i-1}$.

nodes.name: Bound $|S_i|$ via pure edge-/vertex-path counts
nodes.statement: Edge-paths: at most $2i\Delta^{2i-1}$ through a given edge; vertex-paths: $i\Delta^{2i-1}\le 2i\Delta^{2i-1}$. Hence $|S_i|\le 2i\Delta|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|/(1+2^{2/3}\Delta^{-1/3})^{i-1}$.

nodes.name: Sum series and simplify $|F|$
nodes.statement: Combining and summing $\sum_{i\ge1}i x^{i-1}=1/(1-x)^2$ yields $|F|\le\Delta^{5/3}|C_L(G\setminus\{x\})|(2^{-1/3}+8\Delta^{-1/3})$.

nodes.name: Bound on the non-repetitive choice index
nodes.statement: For every graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta$, $\pi'_{\operatorname{ch}}(G)\le\Delta^2+\frac{3}{2^{1/3}}\Delta^{5/3}+8\Delta^{4/3}+1$.
assumptions: $G$ is a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$

nodes.name: Best prior bound on $\pi_{\operatorname{ch}}(G)$ (Montassier et al.)
nodes.statement: $\pi_{\operatorname{ch}}(G)\le\left\lceil\Delta^2+\frac{3}{2^{2/3}}\Delta^{5/3}+\frac{2^{2/3}\Delta^{5/3}}{\Delta^{1/3}-2^{1/3}}\right\rceil$.

nodes.name: General-technique inductive recurrence
nodes.statement: $|c(G)|=\gamma|c(G\setminus\{e\})|-|F|$ with bound $|F|\le\sum_{i\ge1}a_i|c(G\setminus\{e\})|/\alpha^{i-1}$ and constraint $\sum_{i\ge1}a_i/\alpha^{i-1}\le\gamma-\alpha$ giving $|c(G)|\ge\alpha|c(G\setminus\{e\})|$.

nodes.name: Optimal-$\gamma$ formula
nodes.statement: $\gamma=\min_{\alpha>1/r}\left(\alpha+\sum_{i\ge1}a_i/\alpha^{i-1}\right)$, where $r$ is the radius of convergence of $\sum_{i\ge1}a_i x^i$.

nodes.name: Stronger bound implicit in Lemma LP424.2
nodes.statement: Lemma LP424.2 in fact yields $\pi_{\operatorname{ch}}\le\lceil\Delta^2+\frac{3}{2^{2/3}}\Delta^{5/3}+2^{2/3}\Delta^{4/3}-\frac{3}{2^{2/3}}\Delta^{2/3}-2^{2/3}\Delta^{1/3}\rceil$, slightly stronger than Theorem TP424.2.

nodes.name: Tightening the $6\Delta$ bound
nodes.statement: Tightening the last inequality $\frac{15}{4}\ge 3$ yields constant $\gamma=5.21914$ in place of $6$, where $\gamma$ is a root of $-3-4x-20x^2+4x^3$.

nodes.name: Improving the $\Delta^{4/3}$ coefficient in Theorem TP424.5
nodes.statement: A more detailed analysis lowers the coefficient of $\Delta^{4/3}$ to $1+2^{4/3}$ (total coloring) and $2^{4/3}$ (edge coloring).

nodes.name: Bounding non-repetitive (Thue) numbers by maximum degree
nodes.statement: Find tight upper-bounds on $\pi(G), \pi'(G), \pi_{\operatorname{ch}}(G), \pi'_{\operatorname{ch}}(G), \pi_{\operatorname{T_w}}(G), \pi_{\operatorname{T_wch}}(G), \pi_{\operatorname{T}}(G), \pi_{\operatorname{Tch}}(G)$ for graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$.

nodes.name: Lov\'asz Local Lemma (cited)
nodes.statement: Classical probabilistic tool: a family of bad events with bounded local dependency and probabilities meeting LLL's slack condition can be simultaneously avoided.
nodes.origin_citation: Erd\H{o}s and Lov\'asz; algorithmic proof by Moser and Tardos 2010

nodes.name: Alon et al. bound on Thue index (cited)
nodes.statement: $\pi'(G)\in O(\Delta^2)$ where $\Delta$ is the maximum degree of $G$.

nodes.name: Schreyer–\v{S}krabuvl\'akov\'a total Thue bounds (cited)
nodes.statement: $\pi_{\operatorname{T}}(G)\le 5\Delta^2+o(\Delta^2)$, $\pi_{\operatorname{Tch}}(G)\le 17.9856\Delta^2$, and $\pi_{\operatorname{T_w}}(G)\le|E(G)|-|V(G)|+5$.

nodes.name: Thue's theorem on infinite square-free words (cited)
nodes.statement: There exist infinite sequences over three elements that are square-free.
